questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT found in the section of a leaf ?

(A) Guard cells

(B) Stoma

(C) Chlorophyll

(D) Pseudopodia

(E) Xylem
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

 
• **Guard cells:** Guard cells are specialized** cells found in the epidermis of a leaf.** They surround and regulate the opening and closing of stomata, which are tiny pores present on the leaf's surface. The stomata are responsible for gas exchange, allowing carbon dioxide to enter the leaf for photosynthesis and releasing oxygen and water vapor. Therefore, guard cells are indeed found in the section of a leaf.
 
• **Stoma: **As mentioned above, stomata are small pores present in the epidermis of a leaf. They allow the exchange of gases between the leaf and the atmosphere. Stomata are surrounded by the guard cells that regulate their opening and closing. Thus, stomata are indeed found in the section of a leaf.
 
• **Chlorophyll:** Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in chloroplasts, which are organelles within plant cells responsible for photosynthesis. Chloroplasts are mainly found in the mesophyll cells of a leaf, which are located between the upper and lower epidermis. Chlorophyll plays a crucial role in capturing light energy to facilitate photosynthesis. Therefore, chlorophyll is indeed found in the section of a leaf.
 
• **Pseudopodia:** Pseudopodia are temporary projections of the cytoplasm in certain eukaryotic cells, such as amoebas, used for locomotion and capturing prey. However, pseudopodia are not found in the section of a leaf. They are specific to certain single-celled organisms and not a feature of plant cells.
 
• **Xylem:** Xylem is a type of tissue in vascular plants that transports water and some nutrients. While the xylem is found in the plant's stem and root,** it doesn't directly exist in the leaf structure, though leaf veins contain extensions **of the stem's xylem. So it's a bit more ambiguous.

**Therefore the correct answer is pseudopodia and **Xylem **are not found in the section of a leaf. They are a feature of certain single-celled organisms and are not part of the leaf's structure.**

questions.question: The approximate duration of cell cycle of a human cell is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Cell cycle** refers to the series of changes that occur in a newly formed cell. It involves a **cell's growth** and** division** to form **two daughter cells.**

 
• The cell cycle comprises two stages - the **In**terphase and **M phase.**
 
• The** M Phase** represents the phase when the actual **cell division or mitosis occurs**. It is a** short dividing phase.**
 
• **Interphase** represents the phase between two successive M phases. It is a **long non-dividing growing phase.**
 
• Interphase can be divided into 4 steps: Gap 1 (G1), S (synthesis) phase, and Gap 2 (G2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b251078149172c1b03f7d779402e459bab2398e8560645f0902597c44ed91d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **G₁ Phase - **

 
 
• In a human cell, the **G1 phase** of the cell cycle lasts for approximately **11-12 hours.**
 
• During the G1 phase, the **cell is metabolically active** and **continuously grows **but **does not replicate** its DNA.
 
 
 
• **S Phase - **
 
 
• In a human cell, the **S phase** of the cell cycle lasts for about **8 hours**.
 
• **S or synthesis phase** marks the period during which **DNA synthesis or replication** takes place.
 
 
 
• **G₂ Phase** - 
 
 
• The **G****2 **** phase** of the cell cycle lasts for about **4 hours.**
 
• During the **G2 phase**, **proteins are synthesized** in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues. 
 
 
 
• **M Phase**
 
 
• The** M phase** of the cell cycle lasts for about **1 hour **in a human cell.
 
• It is the phase of the cell cycle where **cell division** takes place.
 
 
 
• The​** cell cycle in a human cell** comprising of the Interphase and M phase lasts for a **total time of 24 hours.**

**So the correct answer is option 1 (24 hours).**

questions.question: What is the structure of the chromosome during the Metaphase stage of Cell Division?

options.text: It is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere
It is made up of a number of sister chromatids which are attached to spindle fibres near the centrosome
It is made up of non-sister chromatids attached to a pole of the cell

questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Chromosomes** are rod-shaped, dark-stained bodies that can be seen under a light microscope during the **metaphase stage** of cell division.
 
• Chromosomes contain **DNA** in a highly coiled state.
 
• They carry **genetic information** in the form of** genes **and play an **important role in heredity.**
 
• The number of chromosomes present in an organism is **constant for a particular species.**
 
• Along with the chromosome number, the **size and shape **of individual chromosomes are also constant for a particular species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__​**

 
• Chromosomes are visible under a microscope during the **metaphase stage **of cell division.
 
• During the metaphase stage of the cell division, **chromosome condensation** is completed and thus can be observed clearly under the light microscope.
 
• In the metaphase stage of the cell division, the following **structural features of a chromosome** can be observed under the light microscope:

 
• Chromatid
 
• Chromonema
 
• Chromomeres
 
• Centromere
 
• Nucleolar organizer
 
• Telomere
 
• Satellite

 
• At the metaphase stage, a chromosome is **made up of** **two sister chromatids**.
 
• The two sister chromatids are **held together** by the **centromere**.
 
• The chromosomes at the metaphase stage lie at the **equatorial plane** with **one chromatid** connected by its **kinetochore** to **spindle fibers at one pole.**
 
• Whereas, the **other chromatid** is connected to the spindle fibers of the **opposite pole **by its kinetochore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0ae9dda45494d0eefa8555a1a374726a33409e6df317a5ed493c4a8af683650.png] ​

 

**So, the correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Cisternae is a structure found in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Golgi body**

__Explanation:__

__
 
• The Golgi complex, also known as the Golgi apparatus, is an important cellular organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It is composed of stacks of membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
• The number of cisternae in a stack can vary between different cell types, but there is a typical range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9afbed11c1ec533962143ac2a7526272b100882a608f5e690a8db07ca148200a.png] 

 
• Cisternae in the Golgi Complex:- On average, the number of cisternae per Golgi stack is usually between 3 and 8 cisternae.
 
• The cisternae are organized into distinct regions: the cis-Golgi (entry side), medial-Golgi, and trans-Golgi (exit side).
 
• The processing of molecules occurs sequentially as they move through these regions, with each cisterna containing specific enzymes that perform particular modifications.

**Incorrect Options:**__

 
• **Plasma membrane**: The plasma membrane is a lipid bilayer that surrounds the cell and regulates the entry and exit of substances. It does not contain cisternae.
 
• **Mitochondria**: Mitochondria have two membranes, an outer membrane and an inner membrane, which houses the cristae. The cristae are foldings of the inner membrane that increase the surface area for metabolic processes.
 
• **Plastid**: Plastids are organelles found in plant cells and algae, involved in processes like photosynthesis (chloroplasts) and storage (amyloplasts). They do not contain cisternae.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct for meiosis?

options.text: Meiosis involves single cycle of nuclear and cell division
Doubling of chromosome occur once during S phase
Recombination between sister chromatid of non homologous chromosome

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Pairing of homologous chromosome**

__Explanation:__

 
• Pairing of homologous chromosomes occurs during prophase I of meiosis. This is a crucial step that ensures genetic recombination through crossing over.
 
• Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene stage, which is the third stage of prophase I in meiosis.

**Other options**

 
• **Meiosis involves single cycle of nuclear and cell division:** Incorrect. Meiosis involves two cycles of nuclear and cell division, known as meiosis I and meiosis II.
 
• **Doubling of chromosome occur once during S phase:** During the S phase of the cell cycle, duplication of DNA takes place, not the chromosome
 
• **Recombination between sister chromatid of non homologous chromosome:** Incorrect. Recombination typically occurs between homologous chromosomes, not non-homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids.

questions.question: In which of the following parts genetic material is found
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Nucleus**

__Explanation:__

__
 
• The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells that contains the genetic material of the cell in the form of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).
 
• DNA contains the instructions needed for an organism to develop, survive, and reproduce. It is organized into structures called chromosomes within the nucleus.
 
• The nucleus also controls and regulates the activities of the cell (e.g., growth and metabolism) by controlling gene expression.

**Other Options:**__

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum:** The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a network of membranous tubules within the cytoplasm of a cell, involved in the synthesis, folding, modification, and transport of proteins and lipids. 
 
• **Ribosomes:** Ribosomes are small particles found in large numbers in the cytoplasm of living cells. They are the site of protein synthesis, where they translate genetic information from mRNA to produce proteins. 
 
• **Lysosomes:** Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain digestive enzymes. They are involved in the breakdown of excess or worn-out cell parts, and they play a role in cellular waste disposal.

questions.question: Identify the set of structures found in all types of cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Cell membrane, Ribosome, Cytoplasm**

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Cell membrane:** The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, is a phospholipid bilayer that surrounds the cell. It regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, maintaining the internal environment and enabling communication with other cells.
 
• **Ribosome: **Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis. They read the genetic instructions carried by messenger RNA (mRNA) and translate them into polypeptide chains, which then fold into functional proteins. Ribosomes are found in all cell types, free in the cytoplasm or associated with the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Cytoplasm:** The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the interior of the cell. It contains all the organelles and cell parts, providing a medium through which substances can be transported within the cell. The cytoplasm includes the cytosol (the liquid component) and the organelles suspended in it, except the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.

**Other Incorrect Options:**__

 
• **Nucleus, Ribosome, Cell membrane:** This set is incorrect because prokaryotic cells, such as bacteria, do not have a nucleus. The nucleus is a defining feature of eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Mitochondria, Ribosome, Nucleus:** This set is incorrect because prokaryotic cells lack mitochondria and a nucleus. Mitochondria are present only in eukaryotic cells where they are involved in energy production.
 
• **Chloroplast, Ribosome, Cytoplasm:** This set is incorrect because chloroplasts are unique to plant cells and some algae. Chloroplasts are involved in photosynthesis and are not found in all cell types.

questions.question: Which of the following is surrounded by a double membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Mitochondria and Chloroplasts**

__Explanation:__

__
 
• Organelles are specialized structures within cells that perform specific functions. Some organelles are surrounded by membranes, and the presence of single or double membranes can indicate their structural and functional complexity.
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are often referred to as the "powerhouses" of the cell because they are responsible for energy production through the process of cellular respiration.
 
• They are surrounded by a double membrane: an outer membrane and an inner membrane. The inner membrane is folded into structures called cristae, which increase the surface area for energy production.
 
• The space between the inner and outer membrane is known as the intermembrane space, and the innermost region is called the matrix.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to produce some of their own proteins independently.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69b6acfb9be5a121c5fbae9309e07bf5ff6815985c2a2745815ab7873cc2d1a0.png] 

 
• **Chloroplasts:**

 
 
• Chloroplasts are found in plant cells and some algae, and they are responsible for photosynthesis, the process by which sunlight is converted into chemical energy.
 
• Like mitochondria, chloroplasts are surrounded by a double membrane: an outer membrane and an inner membrane.
 
• Inside the chloroplasts, there are stacks of thylakoids (called grana) and a fluid-filled space called the stroma, where various enzymatic reactions occur.
 
• Chloroplasts also contain their own DNA and ribosomes, enabling them to synthesize some proteins independently.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d87845c88b3fd98297a537de3ccce00a3549eea98e1b008406b7dd0857435949.png] 

*Fig: Sectional view of chloroplast*

**Other Options:**__

 
• **Nuclei and Golgi Apparatus:** The nucleus is surrounded by a double membrane called the nuclear envelope, making it a correct part of this option. However, the Golgi apparatus is not surrounded by a double membrane; it consists of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae
 
• **Ribosomes and Lysosomes:** Ribosomes are not membrane-bound at all; they are made of RNA and protein and are responsible for protein synthesis. Lysosomes are surrounded by a single membrane and contain enzymes for digestion
 
• **Vacuoles and Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum:** Vacuoles are single membrane-bound structures involved in storage and maintaining cell turgor pressure. Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is also surrounded by a single membrane and is involved in protein synthesis and transport.

questions.question: The nucleus is absent in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **bacteria**

**__Explanation:__**

__
 
• A nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells. It contains the cell's genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• Organisms can be broadly classified into prokaryotes and eukaryotes based on the presence or absence of a nucleus. Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus, while eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus.
 
• Bacteria are classified as prokaryotes, meaning their genetic material is not enclosed within a nuclear membrane.

**Other Options:**__

 
• **Algae:** Algae are eukaryotic organisms (except for cyanobacteria, which are often called "blue-green algae" but are actually bacteria). Eukaryotic algae possess a well-defined nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane, making this option incorrect.
 
• **Fungi:** Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that have a true nucleus surrounded by a nuclear membrane. Examples include molds, yeasts, and mushrooms. Since fungi have a nucleus, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Lichens:** Lichens are symbiotic associations between fungi and algae or cyanobacteria. Both fungi and eukaryotic algae in lichens have a true nucleus.

questions.question: Which of the following is not found in animal cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are organelles found in **plant cells** and some algae, but they are absent in animal cells.
 
• These organelles are the site of **photosynthesis**, where sunlight is converted into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
 
• The main pigment in chloroplasts is **chlorophyll**, which gives plants their green color and plays a crucial role in capturing light energy.
 
• Animal cells do not perform photosynthesis and hence lack chloroplasts, relying on other mechanisms for energy production, such as cellular respiration in mitochondria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**: A membrane-bound organelle present in both plant and animal cells that houses genetic material (DNA).
 
• **Ribosomes**: Found in both plant and animal cells; these are the sites of protein synthesis.
 
• **Mitochondria**: Known as the "powerhouse of the cell," mitochondria are found in both plant and animal cells and are responsible for cellular respiration.
 
• **Cell Wall vs. Cell Membrane**: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall in addition to a cell membrane, whereas animal cells only have a cell membrane.
 
• **Vacuoles**: Plant cells usually have a large central vacuole for storage and maintaining cell structure, while animal cells may have smaller, temporary vacuoles.

• A ribosome is the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.concept: Cell, Cell Cycle and Cell Division
questions.question: Crossing-over takes place between:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Cell division is of three types:

 
• Mitosis - Equational division, occurs in somatic (non-sex) cells
 
• Meiosis - Reductional division, occurs in sex cells
 
• Amitosis - Direct type of division, occurs in prokaryotes

 
• Meiosis is the division in which the parent cell divides to form four daughter cells.
 
• Meiosis can be further divided into two stages - Meiosis I and Meiosis II 
 
• Prophase I of Meiosis I has 5 sub-stages
 
• Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene, Diakinesis.

Explanation:__

 
• **Crossing over **refers to the exchange of genetic material between the **non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes**
 
• Crossing over is also known as recombination
 
• It occurs in the **pachytene** stage of** meiosis I **
 
• Crossing over is governed by the enzyme **recombinase**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6ddbe7cc9f05d7c91bbb6f4cde0c4bec5cda2e615534179cc05b5e77ef9a389.png] 

** Diagram showing Crossing over **
